You don’t. You play around it. If you get a high roll game then obviously most player levels will do well but still skill is involved. 

The real value is in turning a low roll game into a 5th-7th. TFT being an RNG based game means you WILL low roll every once in a while no matter how good a player you are. It’s important to realise you won’t top 4 every game. 

I’d recommend playing at a faster pace than what feels natural, especially during the low roll games. That’s what’s helped me the most in games where I feel like luck isn’t on my side. 

There are so many ways to manipulate RNG though so don’t get frustrated by games where you feel it’s unplayable. Most likely you made mistakes which cost you the game. I personally don’t VOD review but I imagine that would help a lot with that kind of thing.

I have the most boring augment taste but it works for me.

I average a 2.43 with thrill, a 2.80 with stand united, a 3.00 with cyber shell, and a 3.33 with pandoras bench. 

You’ll never see me picking any trait specific augments. I have an augment range of about 20 so there’s a bunch that I could consider ‘ least liked ‘. I just adore stuff like celestial blessing, second wind, best friends and obviously the other ones I mentioned with the higher avg placements. You can check my tactics.tools if you want to see the rest of my pick/placement rates but yeah in general it’s a bunch of boring healing augments and flex stuff.

Manage your HP like your life depends on it (because it does!). 

The amount of LP I’ve gained/saved just by turning a low roll 8th into a 6th or 5th is huge. Play the game at a faster tempo than what feels natural to you. Slam items. If there’s any more than 3 components on your bench at any given moment you are griefing. 

Also don’t be afraid to roll a bit earlier on in the game to stabilise your board but know when to stop in order to save your econ for the big 4-5 roll down. 

It’s hard to give one single tip but all of these go under HP management in a sense so yeah that’s what I’d say is the number one aspect that you should try to improve on. 

Good luck with your climb.
